questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience North American academic system and travel the USA

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, however, there were many small things that I was unaware for some reason. So it took me like a whole September to resolve different requirmnet that I could have prepared in August or July but was not informed that early.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived later than the orientation week, so not much assistance. Except when I booked appointments with the coordinator for specific issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dorm housing, where I had a single room but shared bathroom with five people. I believe that other exchange students lived in the hotel nearby, mostly two students sharing a room. I liked my dorm, it was super close to the campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a dining plan, unlimited access to the dining halls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would be aware of the heating. Sometimes it really didn't work, or worked too
much...So
be confident in calling facilities when any problem arises.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were send an email a great deal of time before hand. I had some technical problems with the registration, so it took me a while to resolve them. But you just pick the department and your academic level and add them to your basket, then you can enroll from there, dropping courses was also pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: IT help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful, as I did not need to apply to any specific courses, I aimed for courses that were interesting and matched my graduate level.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Search beforehand, check the professors and course descriptions. 

I would recommend registering for five courses at first instead of the needed four, that way you can drop the one you do not like but still secure a space in the one you prefer better. The first week is always introductory, that way you can see if you like the course/students/professors etc. You have a drop deadline around mid September, so you have time to decide which courses you would like to proceed with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I love the academic system, starting with the grading system, which allows you to work towards the wanted grade the whole semester instead of just writing one big paper at the end of the semester that determines the whole grade. Professors were quite nice, and interesting. Courses were engaging and not boring. I would say if you want great grades, you need to keep up with the all the courses from week-to-week as they likely have a big deal of the grade consisting of attendance/mid-terms/weekly discussions/ weekly assignments or test and etc

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was quite high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More engaging and involved.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Even though I was at the department of Communication, I had mostly electives:
- Marketing and Communication
- Philosophy of Mind
- Dutch Golden Age 
- American Art: Crafting Countercultures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Marketing and Communication, if you want to work on case studies. and Crafting Countercultures if you are into Post-war American Art, very engaging and interesting course, nothing like what I experienced before.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing unexpected but it is more expensive than you imagine, so prepare a well-thought budget plan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport is not something that i was spending on much. I lived next to the campus, so no need to travel to the uni, also there were some bars, beautiful ares, supermarkets and a well-known shopping street in a walking distance. So I really did not spend much on public transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an immense selection of fun clubs, also sport courses that were for free, and drop-in classes that also required no payment. I went to the drop-in classes that included yoga, pilates, indoor cycling and other workouts, I liked them a lot, very nice teachers. Also gym was available from very early to very late.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to find a fun club, that way you will find more American and local friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely explore Boston and Cambridge but also book a cheap bus or sometimes cheap train to New York, it's not that far/

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, many internationals

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved that many were very open. People love making compliments to strangers there :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- plan your budget 
- find a balance between studies and social life (both are fun)
- pack well for winter times (cold and windy)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning lots of interesting and new things, finishing semester as an A student, and traveling much

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing all the fun things out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
